title: Polymorphism without a base class
description:
`Circle`, `Square` and (in the tests) other types have nothing in common except that each has `area()` and `name()`. They share no base class, and you are not allowed to give them one.

Write `class AnyShape`: a single ordinary type that can hold **any** such object and forward the two calls to it. Then `std::vector<AnyShape>` can mix them freely, and `AnyShape` copies like a value.

This is **type erasure**. The standard recipe has three pieces, all private inside `AnyShape`:

1. `struct Concept`: an abstract interface with virtual `area()`, `name()`, and `clone()`.
2. `template <typename T> struct Model : Concept`: holds one `T` and implements the interface by calling the `T`'s own functions.
3. A `std::unique_ptr<Concept>` member.

Public interface:

- a constructor template taking any `T` (stores a `Model<T>`),
- copy constructor and copy assignment (deep copy through `clone()`), move operations,
- `double area() const` and `std::string name() const`.
hints: `Model<T>::clone` is `return std::make_unique<Model>(*this);` It copies the model, and with it the `T` inside.
